---
title: "Exponential distribution"
format: html
filters:
  - shinylive
---

The exponential distribution is a classic choice for modeling continuous quantities such as the waiting time between events. It has one parameter $\lambda>0$ called the **rate**.

## Basic properties

|  |        |
|------|--------------------|
| **Notation** | $X\sim\text{Exponential}(\lambda)$  |
| **Range** | $[0,\,\infty)$ |
| **Parameter space** | $\lambda>0$ |
| **CDF** | $F(x)=\begin{cases}0 & x<0 \\1-e^{-\lambda x}&x\geq 0\end{cases}$ |
| **PDF** | $f(x)=\begin{cases}0 & x<0\\\lambda e^{-\lambda x} &x\geq 0.\end{cases}$ |
| **Inverse CDF** | $F^{-1}(y)=-\frac{\ln(1-y)}{\lambda},0<y<1$ |
| **MGF** | $M(t)=\frac{\lambda}{\lambda-t}$, $t<\lambda$ |
| **Expectation** | $1/\lambda$ |
| **Median** | $(\ln 2)/\lambda$ |
| **Variance** | $1/\lambda^2$ |
| **Moments** | $E(X^n)=\frac{n!}{\lambda^n}$ |

## `R` commands

[Here](https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/stats/html/Exponential.html) is the documentation for the suite of commands that let you work with the exponential distribution in `R`:

```{r}
#| eval: false
dexp(x, rate = 1) # PDF
pexp(q, rate = 1) # CDF: P(X <= q)
qexp(p, rate = 1) # quantile function (inverse CDF)
rexp(n, rate = 1) # random numbers
```

## Play around!

The parameter $\lambda>0$ literally controls the $y$-intercept of the density curve: $f(0)=\lambda$. If you increase $\lambda$, values closer to zero become more likely. If you decrease $\lambda$, values farther from zero become more likely. This is summarized by measures of central tendency like the mean and median, which are *inversely* related to $\lambda$. Furthermore, because this is a unimodal distribution that is *right-skewed*, the skew pulls the mean *above* the median.

You can see all of that below:

```{shinylive-r}
#| standalone: true
#| viewerHeight: 700

library(shiny)

ui <- fluidPage(
  titlePanel("Exponential distribution CDF and PDF"),
  
  sidebarLayout(
    sidebarPanel(
      sliderInput("beta", "Rate (λ):",
                  min = 0.01, max = 2, value = 1, step = 0.01),
      hr(),
      verbatimTextOutput("moments")
    ),
    
    mainPanel(
      plotOutput("gammaPlot", height = "600px")
    )
  )
)

server <- function(input, output) {
  output$moments <- renderText({
    alpha <- 1
    beta  <- input$beta
    mu <- alpha / beta
    sd <- sqrt(alpha) / beta
    paste0("E(X) = ", round(mu, 4),
           "\nmedian(X) = ", round(log(2) / beta, 4),
           "\nsd(X) = ", round(sd, 4))
  })
  
  output$gammaPlot <- renderPlot({
    alpha <- 1
    beta  <- input$beta
    
    # Fixed plotting range
    x_min <- 0
    x_max <- 30
    x <- seq(x_min, x_max, length.out = 2000)
    
    # PDF and CDF
    pdf_vals <- dgamma(x, shape = alpha, rate = beta)
    cdf_vals <- pgamma(x, shape = alpha, rate = beta)
    
    mu <- alpha / beta
    
    # Fixed y-limits
    pdf_ylim <- c(0, 2)
    cdf_ylim <- c(0, 1)
    
    par(mfrow = c(2, 1), mar = c(4, 4, 2, 1))
    
    # --- CDF ---
    plot(c(-3, x), c(0, cdf_vals), type = "l", lwd = 2, col = "blue",
         xlim = c(-2, 25), ylim = cdf_ylim,
         main = "Cumulative Distribution Function (CDF)",
         xlab = "", ylab = "F(x)")
    abline(h = c(0, 1), col = "gray80", lty = 2)
    
    # --- PDF ---
    plot(x, pdf_vals, type = "l", lwd = 2, col = "darkred",
         xlim = c(-2, 25), ylim = pdf_ylim,
         main = "Probability Density Function (PDF)",
         xlab = "x", ylab = "f(x)")
    lines(c(-3, 0), c(0, 0), lwd = 2, col = "darkred")
    text(x = -1, y = beta, labels = expression(lambda))
    
    mtext("E(X)", side = 1, line = 2.2, at = mu, cex = 1.0)
  })
}

shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)


```

## Derivations

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Verify PDF integrates to 1

$$
\begin{aligned}
\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} f(x)\,\text{d}x
&= \int_0^\infty \lambda e^{-\lambda x}\,\text{d}x \\
&= \lambda \int_0^\infty e^{-\lambda x}\,\text{d}x \\
&= \lambda \lim_{b\to\infty} \int_0^b e^{-\lambda x}\,\text{d}x \\
&= \lambda \lim_{b\to\infty}
   \left[-\frac{1}{\lambda}e^{-\lambda x}\right]_0^b \\
&= -\lim_{b\to\infty}
   \left(e^{-\lambda b}-e^0\right) \\
&= -\left(0-1\right) \\
&= 1.
\end{aligned}
$$

:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## From PDF to CDF

$$
\begin{aligned}
F(x)
&= P(X \leq x) \\
&= \int_0^x f(t)\,\text{d}t \\
&= \int_0^x \lambda e^{-\lambda t}\,\text{d}t \\
&= \lambda \int_0^x e^{-\lambda t}\,\text{d}t \\
&= \lambda \left[-\frac{1}{\lambda}e^{-\lambda t}\right]_0^x \\
&= -\left(e^{-\lambda x}-e^0\right) \\
&= 1-e^{-\lambda x}.
\end{aligned}
$$
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## From CDF to PDF

$$
\begin{aligned}
f(x)
&= \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}F(x) \\
&= \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}\left(1-e^{-\lambda x}\right) \\
&= 0-\left(-\lambda e^{-\lambda x}\right) \\
&= \lambda e^{-\lambda x}.
\end{aligned}
$$

:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Quantile function (inverse CDF)

$$
\begin{aligned}
y&= 1-e^{-\lambda x} \\
1-y &= e^{-\lambda x} \\
\log(1-y) &= -\lambda x \\
x &= -\frac{1}{\lambda}\log(1-y).
\end{aligned}
$$
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Compute mean (via definition)

Setup:

$$
\begin{aligned}
E[X]
&= \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} x f(x)\,\text{d}x \\
&= \int_0^\infty x\lambda e^{-\lambda x}\,\text{d}x.
\end{aligned}
$$

Integration by parts:

$$
\begin{aligned}
u &= x,
& \text{d}u &= \text{d}x, \\
\text{d}v &= \lambda e^{-\lambda x}\,\text{d}x,
& v &= -e^{-\lambda x}.
\end{aligned}
$$

Follow through:

$$
\begin{aligned}
E[X]
&= \left[-xe^{-\lambda x}\right]_0^\infty
   + \int_0^\infty e^{-\lambda x}\,\text{d}x \\
&= -\lim_{b\to\infty}\frac{b}{e^{\lambda b}}
   + \frac{1}{\lambda}
   \int_0^\infty \lambda e^{-\lambda x}\,\text{d}x \\
&= -\lim_{b\to\infty}\frac{1}{\lambda e^{\lambda b}}
   + \frac{1}{\lambda}\cdot 1
   \qquad \text{(L'Hôpital's rule)} \\
&= 0+\frac{1}{\lambda} \\
&= \frac{1}{\lambda}.
\end{aligned}
$$

:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Compute variance (via LOTUS)

Setup:

$$
\begin{aligned}
E[X^2]
&= \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} x^2 f(x)\,\text{d}x \\
&= \int_0^\infty x^2\lambda e^{-\lambda x}\,\text{d}x.
\end{aligned}
$$

IBP: 

$$
\begin{aligned}
u &= x^2,
& \text{d}u &= 2x\,\text{d}x, \\
\text{d}v &= \lambda e^{-\lambda x}\,\text{d}x,
& v &= -e^{-\lambda x}.
\end{aligned}
$$

Follow through: 

$$
\begin{aligned}
E[X^2]
&= \left[-x^2e^{-\lambda x}\right]_0^\infty
   + 2\int_0^\infty xe^{-\lambda x}\,\text{d}x \\
&= -\lim_{b\to\infty}\frac{b^2}{e^{\lambda b}}
   + \frac{2}{\lambda}
     \int_0^\infty x\lambda e^{-\lambda x}\,\text{d}x \\
&= -\lim_{b\to\infty}\frac{2b}{\lambda e^{\lambda b}}
   + \frac{2}{\lambda}E[X]
   \qquad \text{(L'Hôpital's rule)} \\
&= -\lim_{b\to\infty}\frac{2}{\lambda^2 e^{\lambda b}}
   + \frac{2}{\lambda}\cdot\frac{1}{\lambda}
   \qquad \text{(L'Hôpital's rule again)} \\
&= 0+\frac{2}{\lambda^2} \\
&= \frac{2}{\lambda^2}.
\end{aligned}
$$

So:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{var}(X)
&= E[X^2] - (E[X])^2 \\
&= \frac{2}{\lambda^2} - \left(\frac{1}{\lambda}\right)^2 \\
&= \frac{2}{\lambda^2} - \frac{1}{\lambda^2} \\
&= \frac{1}{\lambda^2}.
\end{aligned}
$$

:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Compute median



$$
F^{-1}(1/2)=-\frac{\ln(1-1/2)}{\lambda}=-\frac{\ln(1/2)}{\lambda}=\frac{\ln((1/2)^{-1})}{\lambda}=\frac{\ln 2}{\lambda}\approx\frac{0.6931}{\lambda}.
$$
Since $E(X)=1/\lambda$ and $\ln 2<1$, we always have $\text{median}(X)<E(X)$.

:::
